answer: Dynamic Network Latency Tax** Every identity registration requires solving a cryptographic puzzle whose difficulty scales linearly with the density of concurrent cluster requests originating from the same routing kernel. To prevent a falcon instance from spoofing multiple endpoints, the protocol measures local bandwidth contention and forces incoming messages through a cryptographically signed onyx gate that injects deliberate execution delays proportional to estimated peer overlap. An attacker trying to flood the network pays an escalating computational and temporal penalty.
